clue.text: Advance on area of land pointing towards dock

blocks.note: a sub is an advance on wages
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: A piece of land jutting out towards a harbour dock is being developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour, but it is the verb meaning to take away, as in docking pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages is to deduct an amount from them, which is to take it away.

clue.text: Weird scene must involve a session with spiritualist

indicators.note: something weird is out of its normal order, so the letters of scene get rearranged
to involve something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the word as written, to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A strange scene unfolds during a sitting with a medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which a spiritualist medium tries to contact the dead.

clue.text: Livid, boldly confront murderous character

blocks.note: livid originally describes a bluish, bruised colour
to beard someone is to face them defiantly

explanation.surface: Someone furious squares up to a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Livid' reads as angry, but here it is the colour of a bruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebeard is the folk-tale husband who murdered his successive wives.

clue.text: Show plump adult round room

blocks.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A display of a chubby grown-up walking round a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building or hall, typically domed.

clue.text: Slick red coats, possibly semi-formal wear

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements the letters might take

explanation.surface: Smart red coats might pass as semi-formal clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail dress is a short evening dress, the standard semi-formal outfit for parties.

clue.text: Dessert following piece of steak

indicators.note: a piece here is just a small bit, the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Pudding served after a bit of steak.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is British informal for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is colloquial British English for the sweet course that comes after the main meal.

clue.text: Plant on the house is climbing over top of attic

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is turned back to front
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: something on the house costs nothing
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A plant on a house is creeping up over the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a climber on a wall; 'climbing' really reverses the little word, and 'over' places it above the A in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant grown from corms.

clue.text: Weird, last piece of wreckage found in lake

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter
found in says one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Something strange: a last fragment of a wreck turns up in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange in a frightening, unsettling way.

clue.text: Confused royalist living alone

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bewildered monarchist lives on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary describes a person who lives or exists alone, without company.

clue.text: Grown-up daughter wearing gold given by lieutenant

indicators.note: whatever is wearing something has it around it, so one piece is dressed in the other

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An older daughter wears gold jewellery given by an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a person who is fully grown, a grown-up.

clue.text: Foreign car halted leaving place of worship

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters take an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An imported car stops while pulling out of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, a major place of worship.

clue.text: Pretend not to notice poor Enid by Renault

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters come out battered into another order

explanation.surface: Someone pretends not to see poor Enid in her Renault car.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn a blind eye is the idiom for deliberately ignoring something you know about.

clue.text: Conservative has a wager about trendy piece of furniture

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wager goes around the next word

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory bets on a fashionable item of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the political Cabinet; here it is just a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers for storing or displaying things.

clue.text: Appreciation shown by some Lancashire spectators

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used

blocks.note: runs across the end of the county name into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Fans in Lancashire show their admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is esteem or regard for someone's qualities, a form of appreciation.

clue.text: Carol's gone home on motorway in a rage

indicators.note: in places the road abbreviation inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: M is the prefix of British motorways, as in M1

explanation.surface: Carol has left home and is driving the motorway in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is a Christmas song. The M sits between A and ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Away in a Manger is a well-known Christmas carol about the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Sponsor leading exponent

blocks.note: first meaning: a man who sponsors a child at baptism
second meaning: the founding or foremost figure of a movement

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same word: the baptismal sponsor, and the figurative founder, as in the 'godfather of soul'.
explanation.definitionFit: A godfather vouches for a child at christening, and figuratively names the originator or leading figure of a style.

clue.text: Angry over crook bringing weapon

blocks.note: to crook a limb is to bend or bow it

explanation.surface: An irate person confronts a villain who has brought a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' reads as a criminal but is the verb to bend; 'over' puts the first piece above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a bow mounted on a stock that shoots bolts, a medieval weapon.

clue.text: Unscrupulously sold dead rowan tree

indicators.note: acting unscrupulously is acting crookedly, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Someone dishonestly sold off a dead rowan tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowan' looks like the tree being defined, but it is part of the fodder; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Red sandalwood is a tropical tree prized for its red heartwood.

clue.text: Scored briskly? Totally, before e.g. run out

blocks.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A batsman scored quickly before being run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' looks like cricket runs but means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction to play briskly and lively.

clue.text: Not in list of players, one sent to Coventry

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
the cast is the list of actors in a production

explanation.surface: An actor left out of the cast is ostracised.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected by society, just like a person shunned by their peers.

clue.text: Grow furious in diocese about ending of aid

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A clergyman fumes inside the diocese over the end of financial aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is the idiom for becoming suddenly very angry.

clue.text: Ballesteros going round ailing old Spanish port?

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the golfer's name wraps the next word

blocks.note: Seve Ballesteros was the Spanish golfer

explanation.surface: The Spanish golfer plays a round despite being unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Seville sits on the Guadalquivir and was historically Spain's great river port; the question mark flags an inland port.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville was the chief port for Spain's trade with the Americas in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Bottles available in convivial surroundings

indicators.note: available in says the letters can be found within the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Bottles of drink are to be had in a friendly setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Vials are small glass bottles for liquids such as medicine.

clue.text: Very foolish person, fanatic on box

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in fitness nut

explanation.surface: An idiot obsesses over the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' suggests the TV set; it is just a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is slang for a crazy or foolish person.

clue.text: Sweetheart gets frisky at finish of blue film

indicators.note: frisky means playful and lively, so the letters jump about
the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lover gets amorous at the end of a dirty movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue film' suggests something racy, but the film is a classic adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is the Foreign Legion adventure, filmed several times, notably in 1939.

clue.text: Detest gaudy bar house installed

indicators.note: gaudy means garishly showy, so the letters are dressed up differently
something installed is put inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a flashy bar fitted into a house.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to hate or loathe something intensely.

clue.text: Common sense is shown by party after wicket maiden

indicators.note: after says the phrase before it comes later in the answer, so the cricket abbreviation goes first

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A sensible bowler celebrates after taking a wicket in a maiden over.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is sound judgment, the quality of good common sense.

clue.text: Slept around or touched up?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word is wrapped about the next

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether someone slept around or was groped.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is suggestive; 'touched up' simply means repaired, as with a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A restored painting has been repaired and its damaged areas retouched.
